svg.font-family: 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

metadata.orrery:spec: # yaml-language-server: $schema=../references/diagram.schema.json title: Chat system design subtitle: WebSocket gateways keep clients connected; messages go through Kafka to Cassandra and to push providers for offline users direction: down # One port per edge: same-style edges that leave one node (the topic's two outputs, push to APNs and FCM) keep their own lines. layout: { merge: false } legend: solid: Chat traffic dashed: Media transfer # One tier per row, as system design write-ups draw it: the media path and the edge (load balancer, # gateways) under the clients, then the services, the stores and the push providers. `align` puts # each tier's nodes side by side, in the order listed here. nodes: clients: { icon: generic:mobile, label: Clients, note: Mobile and web } media: { icon: generic:bucket, label: Media storage, note: Presigned uploads, align: lb } cdn: { icon: generic:cdn, label: CDN, note: Media downloads, align: lb } lb: { icon: generic:load-balancer, label: Load balancer, note: "L4, Upgrade-aware" } gateway: { icon: logos:websocket, label: WebSocket gateway, note: Open connections, badge: x4, align: lb } chat: { icon: generic:servers, label: Chat service, note: "Ordering, fan-out, presigned URLs" } presence: { icon: generic:server, label: Presence service, note: Heartbeats, align: chat } # Shapes give the whiteboard look: cylinders for stores, a queue for the topic. history: { shape: cylinder, icon: si:apachecassandra, label: Message store, note: Cassandra, align: topic } topic: { shape: queue, icon: logos:kafka-icon, label: messages, note: Kafka topic } status: { shape: cylinder, icon: logos:redis, label: Presence store, note: Redis with TTL keys, align: topic } apns: { icon: tabler:device-mobile-message, label: APNs, note: Apple Push Notification service, align: push } push: { icon: generic:notification, label: Push service, note: Offline users } fcm: { icon: logos:firebase-icon, label: FCM, note: Firebase Cloud Messaging, align: push } edges: # One arrowhead per hop, from the side that opens the connection; WebSocket says it is two-way. - clients -> lb: WebSocket - lb -> gateway -> chat - gateway -> presence -> status - chat -> status: who is online - chat -> history: load history - chat -> topic - topic -> history: persist - topic -> push: notify - push -> apns, fcm - clients --> media: upload - media --> cdn # Written in layout order with the arrow flipped, so the download does not loop back to the first row. - { from: clients, to: cdn, arrow: start, line: dashed, label: download }

svg.title: Chat system design
svg.desc: Chat system design. 13 components. Connections: Clients to Load balancer (WebSocket); Load balancer to WebSocket gateway; WebSocket gateway to Chat service; WebSocket gateway to Presence service; Presence service to Presence store; Chat service to Presence store (who is online); Chat service to Message store (load history); Chat service to messages; messages to Message store (persist); messages to Push service (notify); Push service to APNs; Push service to FCM; Clients to Media storage (upload); Media storage to CDN; Clients to CDN (download).

text.tspan: WebSocket gateways keep clients connected; messages go through Kafka to Cassandra and to push providers for offline users
